# A dashboard a person can arrange

Any page drawn from a `PageDocument` can offer Arrange: a person drags a component by its bar to before or after another, to either side of one to put the two side by side, or onto the end of a container; drags the handle under it to change its height, or at its right edge to change widths. Every drag has a keyboard form (the bar's arrows, arrow keys on the handles), and drags use pointer events, so they work by touch and pen.

Arranging is an option, never a dependency. The page draws the same with it off, and what Arrange sends is the same JSON an agent sends to arrange a page: the order of `children`, `widths` on a `Grid` or `Row`, and `height` or `minHeight`. So a page arranged by hand can be changed by an agent afterwards, and the other way round.

How it works:

- `useArrange` from `@surfaces-ui/spec/react` takes the surface and three functions: `apply` (A2UI messages to take in as one step), `say` (what happened, or why it could not be done) and `remove`.
- `apply` turns the messages into page edits with `editsFromMessages` and applies them with `editPage`, which checks each against the catalog. A move between containers arrives as two components; the edits keep the component that moved.
- Pass `arrange.surfaceFrame` to `SurfaceView` as `frame` and draw `arrange.shown(surface)`, so a size being dragged is drawn as it will be. While arranging, `surfaceFrame` is Arrange's frames; with `resizeWhileViewing: true` it keeps only the size handles while nobody is arranging (between a `Grid`'s or `Row`'s columns, and under a component whose height is set), and each drag is the same one step Arrange would make. Moving and removing stay inside Arrange. Put `arrange.region` on the element around the surface: it quiets the components' own controls so only one layer shows.
- The handles are `ResizeHandle` from `@surfaces-ui/components`, which an app can also place on its own: arrows, Home and End, and Enter or a double click to reset (equal widths, or the height the component chooses).
- `ArrangeToggle`, `ArrangeHelp` and `ArrangeGhost` are the button, the help and status line, and the chip that follows the pointer.

`PageStudio` from `@surfaces-ui/chat` does all of this with `arrange`, logs each arrangement by the person who made it, and tells the agent about it with the next instruction. Use this recipe when the page is not in a studio: a saved dashboard, a report, or any multi-view page of your own.

`ArrangeableDashboard.tsx`:

```tsx
import { type PageDocument, analyticsCatalog, editPage, editsFromMessages, pageSurface, removeComponentMessages } from "@surfaces-ui/spec";
import { ArrangeGhost, ArrangeHelp, ArrangeToggle, SurfaceView, analyticsRenderers, useArrange } from "@surfaces-ui/spec/react";
import { useMemo, useState } from "react";

/**
 * A saved dashboard (a `PageDocument`) a person can rearrange by hand.
 * Arranging is optional: the page draws the same with it off, and an agent
 * arranges the same page by sending the same props (`children`, `widths`,
 * `height`). Every change is one step to undo.
 */
export function ArrangeableDashboard({ initial, onChange }: { initial: PageDocument; onChange?(page: PageDocument): void }) {
  const [history, setHistory] = useState<PageDocument[]>([initial]);
  const page = history.at(-1)!;
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<{ text: string; error?: boolean }>();
  const surface = useMemo(() => pageSurface(page), [page]);

  /** Takes in what Arrange sends, as page edits the catalog checks, and keeps it as one step. */
  const apply = (messages: Parameters<typeof editsFromMessages>[1]) => {
    const { page: next, rejected } = editPage(page, editsFromMessages(page, messages), analyticsCatalog);
    if (rejected.length > 0) return setStatus({ text: rejected[0]!.reason, error: true });
    setHistory((steps) => [...steps, next]);
    onChange?.(next);
  };

  const arrange = useArrange({
    surface,
    apply,
    say: setStatus,
    remove: (id) => {
      const result = removeComponentMessages(surface, id);
      if ("error" in result) setStatus({ text: result.error, error: true });
      else apply(result.messages);
    },
    // Widths and set heights can be dragged without turning Arrange on; moving and removing still need it.
    resizeWhileViewing: true,
  });

  return (
    <section aria-label={page.title}>
      <div>
        <ArrangeToggle arrange={arrange} />
        <button type="button" className="sf-button" disabled={history.length === 1} onClick={() => setHistory((steps) => steps.slice(0, -1))}>
          Undo
        </button>
      </div>
      <ArrangeHelp arrange={arrange} status={status} />
      <div {...arrange.region} className={`sf-container ${arrange.region.className}`}>
        <SurfaceView
          surface={arrange.shown(surface)}
          catalog={analyticsCatalog}
          renderers={analyticsRenderers}
          {...(arrange.surfaceFrame ? { frame: arrange.surfaceFrame } : {})}
        />
      </div>
      <ArrangeGhost arrange={arrange} />
    </section>
  );
}
```

The test draws a real page against `memoryDataSource`, widens a column with the keyboard while viewing, moves a number earlier with its control, removes the title, and undoes the removal. Pointer drags and the resize handles are covered by the playground's browser tests, since jsdom has no layout.

`arrange.test.tsx`:

```tsx
// @vitest-environment jsdom
import { DataSourceProvider } from "@surfaces-ui/components";
import { memoryDataSource } from "@surfaces-ui/data";
import { type PageDocument, analyticsCatalog } from "@surfaces-ui/spec";
import { cleanup, fireEvent, render, screen, waitFor } from "@testing-library/react";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { ArrangeableDashboard } from "./ArrangeableDashboard.js";

afterEach(cleanup);

const sql = "SELECT * FROM orders";
const page: PageDocument = {
  id: "sales",
  title: "Sales",
  catalogId: analyticsCatalog.id,
  components: [
    { id: "root", component: "Column", children: ["title", "numbers"] },
    { id: "title", component: "Text", text: "Sales", variant: "h1" },
    { id: "numbers", component: "Grid", columns: 2, children: ["revenue", "orders"] },
    { id: "revenue", component: "Metric", sourceId: "shop", sql, column: "amount", aggregate: "sum", label: "Revenue" },
    { id: "orders", component: "Metric", sourceId: "shop", sql, aggregate: "count", label: "Orders" },
  ],
};
const data = memoryDataSource({ sourceId: "shop", tables: { orders: [{ id: 1, amount: 10 }, { id: 2, amount: 32 }] } });
const children = (p: PageDocument, id: string) => p.components.find((c) => c.id === id)?.children;

describe("a dashboard a person can arrange", () => {
  it("moves and removes components by their controls, keeps each change as a page edit, and undoes it", async () => {
    const pages: PageDocument[] = [];
    render(
      <DataSourceProvider dataSource={data}>
        <ArrangeableDashboard initial={page} onChange={(next) => pages.push(next)} />
      </DataSourceProvider>,
    );
    // Off by default: the page is drawn as saved, with no frames.
    expect(document.querySelector(".sf-arrange-frame")).toBeNull();

    // While viewing, the line between the two numbers still sizes them: one key press is one step.
    const line = screen.getByRole("separator", { name: "Resize Metric revenue and what is to its right: wider or narrower" });
    expect(line.getAttribute("aria-valuenow")).toBe("50");
    fireEvent.keyDown(line, { key: "ArrowRight" });
    await waitFor(() => expect(pages.at(-1)!.components.find((c) => c.id === "numbers")?.widths).toEqual([0.54, 0.46]));
    fireEvent.keyDown(screen.getByRole("separator", { name: /Resize Metric revenue/ }), { key: "Enter" });
    await waitFor(() => expect(pages.at(-1)!.components.find((c) => c.id === "numbers")?.widths).toEqual([0.5, 0.5]));
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Arrange" }));
    expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Done arranging" })).toHaveProperty("ariaPressed", "true");

    // The same controls a report's tiles have: move "orders" earlier in its grid.
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Move Metric orders earlier" }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(children(pages.at(-1)!, "numbers")).toEqual(["orders", "revenue"]));
    expect(screen.getByRole("status").textContent).toContain('Moved "orders" earlier');

    // Removing takes it off the page, not just out of its container.
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Remove Text title" }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(pages.at(-1)!.components.some((c) => c.id === "title")).toBe(false));
    expect(children(pages.at(-1)!, "root")).toEqual(["numbers"]);

    // Each change was one step.
    fireEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Undo" }));
    await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Remove Text title" })).toBeTruthy());
  });
});
```
